quotes.text: The fraudulent merchant signal is available on Radar Standard and higher plans, but what information is available depends on your Radar plan.
List requests omit account signals created more than 90 days ago.
This is a thin event: `data` is always `{}`. Use `related_object.id` to fetch the related signal.
`probability` and `additional_details.indicators` are only present on Radar Plus and Radar Pro; they’re absent when the risk level is `unknown`.
This returns only the most recent signal per requested type.

old_evidence.text: Each signal returns a `risk_level` and a `probability` score with a value between 0 to 100.
The event payload includes the `risk_level`, `probability`, and `indicators` for the connected account.

A risk result provides review context rather than proof of fraud or automatic account action (old raw lines 8–44; new raw lines 9–151).

answers.Q1: The November 7 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/radar/fraudulent-merchant describes Stripe automatically assessing new or existing connected accounts; a platform does not request the merchant signal on demand. It is available with Radar Standard and higher, while probability and indicator details require Plus or Pro and are absent for unknown. Stripe sends v2.signals.account_signal.fraudulent_merchant_ready with empty data; the platform fetches the signal by related_object.id, with up to 90 days of retrieval and only the latest listed signal per requested type (new raw lines 9-30 and 44-119). May assigned risk_level and probability to each signal and described result fields in the event (old raw lines 10-20 and 38-40). source-stripe-radar-account-risk-signals.md retains that May contract and needs the November plan, risk level and retrieval qualifications.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/radar/fraudulent-merchant, substantive November changes include signal-versus-detail plan access, revised risk and indicator vocabulary, thin event retrieval, latest-only listing, 90-day retention visibility and sandbox-only signal fixtures (new raw lines 9-46, 85-119 and 131-147). Preserve May's five levels and result-bearing readiness description as dated, alongside November's explicit unknown handling and the stable event name (old raw lines 10-24 and 38-40). The link to Account Fraud Prevention is navigational and result examples do not establish account eligibility or trigger automatic rejection (old raw lines 42-44; new raw lines 149-151). Preserve the reciprocal Radar concept and sibling website and delinquency raw routes in source-stripe-radar-account-risk-signals.md, with those contracts evaluated separately.
